title: Deuteronomy Bible Quiz - Chapter 20
description: Ten questions on Deuteronomy 20: the priest's words before battle, who may go home, and the rules for a siege.

questions.text: Why should Israel not be afraid of an enemy army larger than their own?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says they shall not be afraid, for Yahweh their God, who brought them up out of Egypt, is with them.

answers.text: Because Yahweh their God is with them
Because the enemy had no king

questions.text: Who was to approach and speak to the people when they drew near to battle?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says that when they draw near to the battle, the priest shall approach and speak to the people.

questions.text: Which of these men were the officers to tell to go home before the battle?
questions.explanation: The officers were to tell the man who has planted a vineyard and has not used its fruit to go and return to his house.

answers.text: A man who owned many cattle
A man who had fought in battle before
A man who had planted a vineyard and not used its fruit
A man who was the oldest son in his family

questions.text: Why was a fearful and faint-hearted man sent home?
questions.explanation: The officers were to say: "Let him go and return to his house, lest his brother's heart melt as his heart."

answers.text: So that he would not run away during the battle
So that the enemy would not see him
So that he could guard the camp
So that his brother's heart would not melt like his

questions.text: Whom did the officers appoint after they finished speaking to the people?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says they shall appoint captains of armies at the head of the people.

questions.text: What were the Israelites to do first when they drew near to a city to fight against it?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says: "then proclaim peace to it."

answers.text: Offer a sacrifice before its gates

questions.text: What would happen to the people of a city that answered with peace and opened to Israel?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says all the people found in it shall become forced laborers and serve Israel.

answers.text: They would be set free to leave

questions.text: Which of these peoples is named in the list of verse 17?
questions.explanation: Verse 17 names the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite.

questions.text: Why were these peoples to be utterly destroyed, according to verse 18?
questions.explanation: It was so that they would not teach Israel to follow all their abominations done for their gods, and so cause Israel to sin.

answers.text: So they would not teach Israel their abominations
Because their cities were too strong
So Israel could take their horses

questions.text: During a long siege, which trees were not to be cut down?
questions.explanation: They were not to destroy the trees they could eat of; only trees known not to be for food could be cut down.

answers.text: Trees whose fruit they could eat
Trees taller than the city wall
